suggestions.title: Empty HTML comments `<!-->` / `<!--->` are treated as unclosed and hide every later evidence link
suggestions.failurePath: PR body `<!--> see https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/<40-hex>/docs/verify/1404/a.txt`. visibleText starts the close search at open+4, so the `-->` inside `<!-->` (index 2) or `<!--->` (index 3) is skipped. With no later `-->`, the rest of the body is dropped: links=[] and others=[] (reproduced). cmark-gfm ends an HTML block on a line that contains `-->` counting from the line start, and browsers treat `<!-->` as an empty comment, so GitHub shows the link. The gate would report a missing evidence link for a body that has one. This fails closed, not open.

suggestions.title: Same evidence file recorded twice when the owner's case or the percent-encoding differs
suggestions.failurePath: Body links `.../xiechimon/pacman/<sha>/docs/verify/1404/a.txt` and `.../XiechiMon/Pacman/<sha>/docs/verify/1404/%61.txt`. `seen` is keyed on the raw URL text before the owner is case-folded and the path decoded, so `links` holds two identical {sha, path:'docs/verify/1404/a.txt'} entries (reproduced). The PR claims each file is recorded once. A future caller that counts links or reports per link would double count. Keying `seen` on `${sha}/${path}` after validation would fix it.

This matches pr-gate's EVIDENCE_RE /i, and the PR's Risk section covers only the digest side, so it is a parity choice to note, not a regression.

suggestions.title: Protected-path matching folds case ASCII-only: names with U+017F (long s) or U+212A (Kelvin sign) pass SAFE_PATH and escape D4 classes
suggestions.failurePath: globToRegExp builds patterns with the 'i' flag but without 'u'. In that mode JS does not fold U+017F to 's' or U+212A to 'k'. SAFE_PATH (line 48) allows any \p{L}, so both characters pass it. classifyPaths then reports 'apps/server/src/ſcripts/x.sh', 'apps/web/src/AGENTſ.md' and 'packages/x/src/pacKage.json' as auto-mergeable and not protected. ADR 0021 D4 gives case-insensitivity because the macOS default filesystem ignores case. If that filesystem applies Unicode case folding, these names resolve to scripts/, AGENTS.md and package.json on a macOS checkout, for example on the user's daemon machines. On Linux CI and on GitHub the names stay distinct, so CI checks are not affected. Not reachable at this head because nothing calls classifyPaths. The fix is the 'iu' flag on line 38 (the escape set is valid under u). pr-gate.js on #1410 uses the same matcher.
suggestions.evidence: node: new RegExp('^(?:.*/)?scripts/.*$','i').test('apps/server/src/ſcripts/x.sh') === false; the same pattern with 'iu' === true; SAFE_PATH.test(...) === true for both sample names. I did not verify APFS folding behaviour for U+017F and U+212A.

suggestions.title: Gate reads its D4 lists through the @pacman/shared star re-exports, which an auto-mergeable file can shadow
suggestions.failurePath: paths.ts and digest.ts import AUTO_MERGE_PATH_GLOBS, PROTECTED_PATH_GLOBS and MERGE_GATE_SOURCE_GLOBS from '@pacman/shared'. That package resolves to packages/shared/src/index.ts, which does `export * from './records/index.js'`, which does `export * from './merge-gate.js'` (records/index.ts, added in this PR). Under ESM a local export takes precedence over a star export without any error, so a PR adding `export const PROTECTED_PATH_GLOBS = [] as const` to packages/shared/src/index.ts would empty the protected classes. That file is under packages/*/src/**, which is auto-mergeable and outside class 4. Not reachable at this head (no caller, and the policy is always human). The ticket already tracks it in comment 6310264292: before P4 the two index files join class 4, or the gate imports from records/merge-gate.ts directly.

suggestions.title: Python cross-check sorts by code point, so it does not independently pin the UTF-16 code-unit order
suggestions.evidence: crosscheck2.py uses Python's default sorted() on str, which orders by code point. digest.ts relies on JS default sort, which orders by UTF-16 code unit. The two orders differ only when a name has a supplementary-plane character next to one in U+E000-U+FFFF. All test vectors and the fixture are ASCII, so they agree there. My own recomputation with an explicit UTF-16 key gives the same fixture digest.
suggestions.failurePath: The round 4/5 claim 'the code-unit sort against a digest computed in Python' holds only for BMP-below-surrogate names. A name such as one mixing an emoji and a CJK compatibility character would sort differently in the reference than in digest.ts, and the cross-check would not catch a regression there. Use key=lambda s: s.encode('utf-16-be') in the reference, or narrow the claim.
